title: Edmund and the Sigil
premise: Sebastian Delacroix, a cartographer hiding her magic in a city that has outlawed it, discovers that the king who ordered the purge of the gifted is not the king at all—he is Edmund, the true heir, bound and buried beneath a sigil while a shape-shifting usurper wears his face and crown. Recruited by a dying loyalist, Sebastian must map her way into the palace's sealed heart and unbind the sigil before the usurper completes a rite that will make his stolen crown permanent. Along the way she falls for Edmund in his weakened, mortal form, forcing her to choose between the rebellion's cold arithmetic and her own heart. In the end she unbinds Edmund at the cost of her own gift, and the two of them expose the usurper together—she with truth and testimony, he with the crown he never wanted.
about_author: Ines Winterbourne is a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three libraries and lost herself in a fourth. She writes fantasy from a coastal town where the fog, she insists, is doing most of the plotting.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Lie
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She sells a love charm to a desperate noblewoman while hiding her own gift beneath cartographic tools and careful anonymity. When the crown posts the first bounty notices for the gifted, her oldest client is dragged into the street. Emotional beat: the fragile safety of invisibility shattering.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Map
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A wounded old courtier, Lord Averil, finds her through her charms and reveals the truth: the king is a prisoner, and Sebastian's own maps—drawn in a trance she never understood—chart the palace's hidden sigil-rooms. He dies before finishing. Emotional beat: reluctant inheritance of a dangerous mission.

chapters.title: The Face in the Mirror Room
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, slipping into the palace as a hired surveyor. She witnesses the 'king' shed his human face for a moment in a mirrored corridor—and realizes the usurper is a bound spirit wearing Edmund's shape. Emotional beat: horror, and the vertigo of knowing too much.

chapters.title: Edmund
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Beneath the palace, in a cell woven from his own name, the true king has kept his mind alive for seven years by drawing maps of places he remembers. He feels someone tracing his sigil-rooms and dares, for the first time, to hope. Emotional beat: loneliness cracking open.

chapters.title: What the Gift Costs
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She finds the cell but cannot break the sigil without a power she has never dared use fully. Edmund, weak and mortal, begs her to leave him and save the city instead. She refuses. Emotional beat: the first sparks of love against all sense.

chapters.title: The Hunt Closes
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The usurper's inquisitors trace Averil's contacts; Sebastian's safehouses burn one by one. Her rebel allies urge her to abandon Edmund—the mission, they argue, was never about the man. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth, and the cost of choosing.

chapters.title: The Rite of the Unworn Crown
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She learns the usurper's plan: on the solstice he will bind the sigil permanently, erasing Edmund's name from every record and memory. Time collapses to days. Emotional beat: desperation sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Solstice in the Sealed Heart
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Sebastian fights her way to the sigil-room as the rite begins; Edmund, half-unbound, drags himself through the palace's memory-warping corridors to meet her. They reach the sigil together as the usurper arrives wearing the king's face. Emotional beat: climax—love and duty fused into one act.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. To break the sigil she must pour her entire gift into it, knowing she will never draw or charm again. She does it. Edmund rises, mortal and name-restored, and confronts the usurper, who unravels when the court is forced to look at the true king. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into triumph.

chapters.title: A Map of Ordinary Places
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, months later. Magic is decriminalized; Edmund, a reluctant king, offers Sebastian her gift back through a court rite, and she must decide who she is without it. She chooses to remain a cartographer—of real places, with him. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed, love chosen freely.
